findings.title: A privacy notice is published and reachable from the website
findings.rationale: no privacy or data-protection page could be found on the site
findings.remediation: Publish a DPDP notice at /privacy-policy and link it from the footer of every page, the admission enquiry form and the fee portal.
findings.school_note: Checked by locating a policy page during the crawl.

findings.title: The notice itemises the categories of personal data collected
findings.rationale: no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: List each category actually collected: student name, date of birth, photograph, Aadhaar-linked APAAR/UDISE identifiers, parent contact, medical and allergy notes, transport pickup point, biometric attendance, CCTV footage, fee and bank details.

findings.title: The notice states the specified purpose for each category
findings.rationale: no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Set out a table of category against purpose, and drop any category with no purpose behind it.

findings.title: The notice explains how to withdraw consent
findings.rationale: no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Add a withdrawal paragraph naming the channel - a link, an email address, or the school office - and state that withdrawal does not affect processing already carried out lawfully.

findings.title: The notice explains Data Principal rights and how to exercise them
findings.rationale: no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Name the four rights, give one channel to exercise all of them, and publish the period within which the school will respond.

findings.title: The notice gives the route to complain to the Data Protection Board
findings.rationale: no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Add: 'If your grievance is not resolved, you may complain to the Data Protection Board of India.' State that the school's own grievance route must be exhausted first.

findings.title: Consent is collected by clear affirmative action, not assumed
findings.rationale: consent appears to be assumed rather than taken by a clear affirmative action; self-assessed: partly
evidence: implied-consent wording found: by continuing to use
findings.remediation: Replace any implied-consent banner with an unticked checkbox beside a link to the notice, and log the consent artefact.

findings.title: Only data necessary for the stated purpose is collected
findings.rationale: 3 public form field(s) ask for a sensitive or identifier category; each needs a stated purpose or removal
findings.remediation: Review every public form field against its purpose and delete the fields that cannot be justified.

findings.title: Consent records are kept and are auditable
findings.rationale: self-assessed: no
findings.remediation: Add a dated, signed DPDP consent block to the admission form and keep a register mapping student to consent version.

findings.title: Verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data
findings.rationale: self-assessed: no. no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Capture parental consent against a verified parent identity - details already held in the admission record, or a virtual token from an authorised entity such as a DigiLocker provider - and retain the verification evidence.
findings.school_note: Rule 12 with Part A of the Fourth Schedule relieves an educational institution of s.9(1) for academic activities and student safety. It does not relieve the school for anything else - alumni marketing, photographs in promotional material, an EdTech app the school resells, or a third-party feed.

findings.title: No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising to children
findings.rationale: 2 advertising, social or session-recording scripts from 1 host load on a site aimed at children and their parents
findings.remediation: Remove advertising and social pixels from all pages. Keep only analytics that is necessary and configured without advertising features, and document the safety or academic purpose relied on.
findings.school_note: The Fourth Schedule exemption covers tracking and behavioural monitoring for academic activity and for the safety of enrolled students. A Meta or DoubleClick pixel on a public page serves neither purpose and sits outside the exemption.

findings.title: Reliance on the Fourth Schedule exemption is documented and purpose-limited
findings.provision: Rule 12 read with Fourth Schedule, Part A
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Record, per processing activity, whether it is academic, safety or neither; for the 'neither' column, obtain verifiable parental consent.

findings.title: Student photographs and names are not published without consent
findings.rationale: the site carries pages or embeds likely to publish images of identifiable children; confirm a media consent covers each one; self-assessed: no
evidence: pages likely to carry student images: http://127.0.0.1:8931/gallery.html
findings.remediation: Take a separate, revocable media consent at admission, keep a do-not-publish list, and honour it across website, brochures and social media.

findings.title: The site and its forms are served over HTTPS
findings.rationale: a form posts personal data to a plain http:// address
findings.remediation: Install a TLS certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and confirm no form posts to an http:// action.

findings.title: Reasonable security safeguards are in place and documented
findings.rationale: self-assessed: partly
findings.remediation: Write a one-page security standard covering access control on the ERP, encryption of exports, a one-year log retention setting and a tested backup.

findings.title: A personal data breach response procedure exists
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Adopt a breach procedure naming who declares a breach, the notification templates for parents and for the Board, and a breach register.

findings.title: A retention schedule exists and data is erased when the purpose ends
findings.rationale: self-assessed: no. no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
findings.remediation: Set a period per record class - unsuccessful enquiries, withdrawn students, alumni, CCTV, biometric attendance - and schedule the deletion. Keep only what a records rule requires.

findings.title: CCTV and biometric data are handled under a stated rule
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Fix a CCTV overwrite cycle, restrict who can export footage, log every export, and confirm the biometric vendor's contract and deletion terms.

findings.title: Contact details of the person answering data questions are published
findings.rationale: contact addresses are published but none is identifiable as the data-protection or grievance contact
findings.remediation: Name a role - not an individual's personal mobile - publish a dedicated address such as dpo@school.edu.in on the policy page and the contact page, and route it to a monitored inbox.

findings.title: A grievance redressal mechanism with a stated response period
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Publish the grievance route and a response period, and keep a dated register of requests and outcomes.

findings.title: A record of processing activities exists
findings.rationale: self-assessed: no
findings.remediation: Build a register of every system holding student or staff data - ERP, transport GPS, biometric, CCTV, LMS, WhatsApp groups, exam portal - with owner, purpose, categories and vendor.

findings.title: Staff who handle student data have been trained
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Run a short annual briefing for teaching and office staff, and issue a one-page rule on sharing student data.

findings.title: A written contract is in place with every data processor
findings.rationale: self-assessed: no
findings.remediation: Add a data-processing addendum to each vendor agreement covering purpose limitation, security, sub-processing, breach reporting and deletion on exit.

findings.title: Third-party trackers on the website are disclosed and justified
findings.rationale: 2 third-party tracker host(s) load but none is named in the published policy
findings.remediation: Inventory the scripts, remove what is not needed, name the rest in the notice, and gate non-essential ones behind consent.

findings.title: Cross-border transfer position is known
findings.rationale: this cannot be seen from a website; answer it in the internal-practices questionnaire
findings.remediation: Ask each vendor in writing where student data is hosted and record the answer.

perspectives.title: Verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data
agreed_facts: self-assessed: no. no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
perspectives.institution_position: Part A of the Fourth Schedule relieves an educational institution of section 9(1) for academic activities and for the safety of enrolled students. Teaching a child and keeping them safe is the whole of what the school does with their data, and the obligation does not commence until 14 May 2027 in any event.
perspectives.regulator_position: The exemption is conditional and purpose-bound. It does not reach a prospective student who has not enrolled, an alumni database, a promotional photograph, or an EdTech product the school resells. For anything outside those purposes the school needs verifiable parental consent, with due diligence under Rule 10 that the consenting adult is identifiable - not merely whoever filled in the form.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether the school can name, for a given consent, how it knew the person consenting was the parent. 'The form came back signed' is not verification.

perspectives.title: No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising to children
agreed_facts: 2 advertising, social or session-recording scripts from 1 host load on a site aimed at children and their parents
perspectives.institution_position: Analytics helps the school understand what parents look for on the site and improve it. The Fourth Schedule expressly permits tracking and behavioural monitoring by an educational institution.
perspectives.regulator_position: The Fourth Schedule permits tracking for academic activity and for the safety of enrolled students. An advertising pixel serves neither: it exists to build an advertising profile of the visitor for a commercial third party. Section 9(3) is a prohibition, not a balancing exercise, and a school website's visitors are children and their parents.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Look at what each script is for, not what the school uses it for. An advertising or social pixel cannot be brought inside 'academic' or 'safety' by intention. Removing it takes ten minutes and settles the point.

perspectives.title: A privacy notice is published and reachable from the website
agreed_facts: no privacy or data-protection page could be found on the site
perspectives.institution_position: The school publishes its material information through the prospectus, the admission form and circulars. A parent who enrols has the information in practice, and the website is not the only notice channel. Rule 3, which prescribes the notice format, does not commence until 14 May 2027.
perspectives.regulator_position: Section 5 is an obligation of the Act, in force since enactment, and the Rules do not defer it. Notice must accompany the request for consent. A prospectus handed over once at admission does not reach the enquirer who fills in a web form and never enrols - yet their data is collected all the same.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether a parent or an enquirer can, today, open one document that says what is collected, why, how to withdraw and how to complain. If no such document exists, the argument does not survive contact with the question.

perspectives.title: A retention schedule exists and data is erased when the purpose ends
agreed_facts: self-assessed: no. no policy text could be read, so this could not be assessed from the website
perspectives.institution_position: School records must be retained. CBSE requirements, transfer certificates and the possibility of a former student needing a document years later all demand it.
perspectives.regulator_position: Retention required by law is permitted; indefinite retention of everything is not. The records that matter here are the ones no rule requires - enquiries from parents who never enrolled, CCTV from three years ago, biometric templates of students who left. Section 8(7) requires erasure once the purpose is spent.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether a written schedule exists naming a legal basis for each period, and whether anything has actually been deleted under it in the past year. A schedule never acted on is a document, not a control.

perspectives.title: A written contract is in place with every data processor
perspectives.institution_position: The school buys standard products from established vendors on the vendors' own terms. A school of this size has no bargaining power to rewrite a national vendor's contract.
perspectives.regulator_position: Section 8(2) permits engagement of a processor only under a valid contract. Limited bargaining power is a commercial fact, not a legal defence - it is a reason to ask, to choose a different vendor, or to record the risk the school has knowingly accepted. Most vendors now have a data-processing addendum ready and will send it if asked.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether a signed data-processing clause exists for each vendor holding student data. This is a document-production question, not an argument.

perspectives.title: Consent is collected by clear affirmative action, not assumed
agreed_facts: consent appears to be assumed rather than taken by a clear affirmative action; self-assessed: partly
implied-consent wording found: by continuing to use
perspectives.institution_position: The admission process is consensual. Parents sign the admission form knowing the school will process the student's data, and the processing is necessary to deliver the service they sought.
perspectives.regulator_position: A signature on an admission form is consent to admission, not specific and informed consent to each purpose. Section 6(1) requires a clear affirmative action. A pre-ticked box, a 'by continuing you agree' banner, and silence are each expressly not that. Bundled consent is the classic failure.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether the school can produce, for a named student, the consent artefact and show which purposes it covered. If it cannot be produced, it cannot be relied on.

perspectives.title: Student photographs and names are not published without consent
agreed_facts: the site carries pages or embeds likely to publish images of identifiable children; confirm a media consent covers each one; self-assessed: no
pages likely to carry student images: http://127.0.0.1:8931/gallery.html
perspectives.institution_position: Publishing achievements is what schools do, parents are proud of it, and nobody has ever objected. The photographs celebrate the children rather than exploiting them.
perspectives.regulator_position: A named, identifiable child on a public web page is processing of a child's personal data for a promotional purpose. No academic or safety exemption reaches promotion. Absence of objection is not consent, and the one parent who does object - often for a reason they should not have to explain, such as a custody arrangement - needs the school to have a mechanism ready.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Whether a separate, revocable media consent exists, and whether a do-not-publish list exists and is actually checked before a photograph goes up.

perspectives.title: The site and its forms are served over HTTPS
agreed_facts: a form posts personal data to a plain http:// address
perspectives.institution_position: The website is a brochure site hosted on a standard commercial package. It holds nothing sensitive and the hosting provider manages security.
perspectives.regulator_position: The form on that brochure site collects a child's name, date of birth and a parent's phone number, and posts them across the network in the clear. Encryption in transit is the least that section 8(5) can mean, it costs nothing, and every browser now marks the page as not secure to the parent filling it in.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Open the page and look at the address bar. This is the cheapest finding on the list to close and the most conspicuous to leave open.

perspectives.title: A record of processing activities exists
perspectives.institution_position: The school knows what systems it runs. The ERP, the biometric machine and the transport app are hardly secret, and listing them changes nothing about how they operate.
perspectives.regulator_position: Section 8(1) makes the school accountable for all processing, including through processors. Nothing can be governed that has not been listed, and the systems that surface only when the list is drawn up are the dangerous ones - the exam portal a teacher signed up for, the WhatsApp groups holding parent numbers, the old laptop with the fee database on it.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Sit down and write the list. What you discover in the last twenty minutes of writing it is the reason the obligation exists.

perspectives.title: Third-party trackers on the website are disclosed and justified
agreed_facts: 2 third-party tracker host(s) load but none is named in the published policy
perspectives.institution_position: The scripts on the website are standard tools that every site uses. The school did not choose them individually; the web designer installed them.
perspectives.regulator_position: Every third-party script loading on a school page discloses the visitor's data to that third party. Sections 5 and 6 require them to be named in the notice and consented to, and the school - not the web designer - is the Data Fiduciary answerable for them.
perspectives.what_decides_it: Compare the list of scripts the scan found against the list named in the policy. The difference is the finding.
